First, you need lots of money to lend to people. You can do this by borrowing money from people at a lower rate than you lend it out.

Second, you have to be able to cover the likely withdrawals of the people you have borrowed from, while still making profit on the money you are lending out.

Easy Peasy ;)

You need government approval, in the US, that means a state or federal charter (depending on where you want to operate your bank).

This is the application form for most federal charters.

Note that there are few specific requirements and lots of evaluations. You'll generally need between $10 and $20 million in capital (investments not deposits), a plan to serve some community (bonus points if it's undeserved currently), a good attorney (ideally someone with regulator experience), and a wider shareholder base helps considerably (because regulators expect those shareholders to become clients of the bank, too).
